chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: Textual trust requires relative confidence that the original wording remains locatable in the manuscripts, rather than absolute certainty about every disputed reading.

orphanFallback.rationale: The passage independently defines Wallace's probabilistic standard and affirms that the original wording remains available in the manuscript tradition.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-03.proposition: The raw number of textual variants largely reflects the unusually large manuscript base, which produces both more recorded differences and more evidence for reconstruction.

orphanFallback.rationale: The manuscript totals and extensive textual coverage independently explain why a high variant count is compatible with, and partly caused by, abundant evidence.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: Numerous New Testament witnesses from the first three centuries collectively preserve extensive textual coverage and compare favorably with the sparse remains of classical authors.

orphanFallback.rationale: The counts, dates, collective coverage, and comparison with classical remains affirmatively establish the unusual evidentiary strength of the witness base.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: Later New Testament manuscripts add only a limited amount of material to a substantially attested text, unlike many classical works surviving partially or across much larger gaps.

orphanFallback.rationale: The limited accumulation of additional material over centuries and the comparison with incomplete classical works independently support broad transmissional continuity.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: More than ninety-nine percent of textual variants make virtually no difference because many consist of spelling, word-order, inflectional, or otherwise untranslatable differences.

orphanFallback.rationale: The concrete linguistic examples independently show why formally distinct Greek readings can preserve the same translated meaning and therefore have little significance.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Fewer than one percent of variants are both meaningful and viable, although hundreds of disputed passages can still affect interpretation to some degree.

orphanFallback.rationale: The passage independently distinguishes the small meaningful-and-viable subset from the total while expressly preserving the reality of interpretation-sensitive disputes.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: No viable manuscript variant has been shown to place an essential Christian belief expressed elsewhere in the New Testament in jeopardy.

orphanFallback.rationale: The distinction between genuine interpretive disputes and threats to essential beliefs independently limits the consequences claimed for viable variants.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: New Testament copying was not serial degradation because written branches, access to earlier witnesses, patristic commentary, and repeated consultation of originals supplied independent checks.

orphanFallback.rationale: The identified features of written, branching transmission independently provide mechanisms by which earlier wording could persist and copying errors could be detected.

chunk-003:c003-01.proposition: The close agreement of Papyrus 75 and Codex Vaticanus, despite neither being copied from the other, supports a shared textual ancestor reaching into the early second century.

orphanFallback.rationale: The dating, independence, and unusually close agreement of the two manuscripts directly supply affirmative evidence for an earlier stable textual tradition.

chunk-003:c003-02.proposition: The standard critical Greek text treats the original wording as surviving among extant manuscript readings in virtually every disputed location.

orphanFallback.rationale: The comparison between tens of thousands of listed variants and very few proposed conjectural locations independently supports recovery from surviving readings.

chunk-003:c003-08.proposition: Comparison among error-filled descendant copies can reconstruct their exemplar, while identifiable incidental errors do not by themselves prevent recovery of an earlier text.

orphanFallback.rationale: The reconstruction exercises and evidence concerning identifiable early manuscript errors independently demonstrate how comparison can recover a predecessor text.

chunk-004:c004-07.proposition: Historical trust in ancient texts properly rests on probability rather than certainty, because consistently demanding radical certainty would undermine knowledge of ancient literature generally.

orphanFallback.rationale: The comparison with ordinary inquiry into Greco-Roman literature independently justifies a moderate probabilistic standard for evaluating ancient textual evidence.
